Smaller, with readable rows?

Yes, at the accepted 9pt Impact size. Each 600px row fits a 450pt document text measure. The full 840px PNG includes large white margins and is 8.75 inches across if inserted at 96px/in; use the actual Letter PDF or RTF for page layout. A 550px field with 9pt type and a 500px field with 7.5pt type also read in Vision, but have no phone acceptance yet. At 12pt, the tested 600px field failed; the successful two-line-per-region layout needed 800px of body width. Smaller field, larger letters and enough QR-region ink compete with one another.

All caps required?

No. The accepted smaller story preserves ordinary mixed case. A lowercase version also read in Vision. Case changes still alter letter shapes and ink distribution: Georgia and Arial Black uppercase examples read where their tested mixed-case counterparts failed.

Other fonts?

Impact, Avenir Next Condensed and PT Sans Narrow have positive native Vision examples. The tested Arial, Helvetica Neue, DIN Condensed and several Georgia/Arial Black mixed-case settings failed. This is a measured set of recipes, not a ranking of every font. Impact is intrinsically heavy even when its CSS weight says “Regular”; requesting bold on the same installed face often changed no pixels.

How close can the ink be?

For the tested mixed-case Impact fixture, black/gray160 read; gray152 and gray144 failed. Black32/gray180 read, a 148-level difference; black64/gray180 failed. Avenir Heavy/Regular with black/gray96 read. Avenir Heavy/UltraLight worked with zero RGB difference because the weight difference still supplies strong ink-density separation. There is no universal numeric threshold: font shape, weight, wrapping, payload and native rendering all matter.

Can lighter letters be Regular?

Yes, in the Avenir black-Heavy/gray96-Regular recipe. Both weights black failed in the earlier Heavy/Regular test. The all-black accepted recipe uses UltraLight. Impact also works with both requested weights set to Regular when color provides the separation. Uniform weight plus uniform color removes the intended per-letter QR signal; ordinary plain TXT does not preserve these QR styles.

Can I use my own words?

The new generator wraps whole words, keeps case and punctuation, and never substitutes a letter bank. Four complete-copy Avenir black HTML word streams—original, a new story, narrow-letter-heavy prose and broad-letter-heavy prose—read in Vision. The comparable Impact outputs were mixed: four of six new word/payload cases read. Reflowing the same words can change the result. This is promising support for varied prose, while arbitrary prose remains unproven. Short paragraphs need explicit repetition to fill this dense fifty-row layout; one 1,136-word source also worked once with repetition disabled.

Distance, resolution and paste?

You reported finding the right phone distance, and the original HTML needed a distant, zoomed-out view. A working explanation is that the reader needs to see the overall pattern through the gaps between letters; we did not trace the camera's internal pipeline. Native 2× HTML rendering read in Vision while 3× failed. Actual TextEdit HTML transfer changed font size or line spacing. Even a corrected 9pt, fifty-row paste failed to decode. Source selection, downloadable RTF, actual paste, phone scanning and print remain separate checks.

An operational local starting point

Your words, exact payload, visible letters.

1 · Open the workbench locally.

It is one offline HTML file with the existing pinned encoder and license. No AI, account, upload or server is required. Start with the exact saved example to establish your viewing setup.

2 · Enter your prose and exact link.

Choose Impact, black Heavy/UltraLight Avenir, or Heavy/gray-Regular Avenir. Keep complete-source repetition enabled for a short paragraph; turn it off for a long source you want used once. Generation rejects overflow, missing fonts and impossible spacing.

3 · Save the recipe and source.

Raw source TXT and recipe preserve original whitespace. Displayed text normalizes whitespace into whole-word rows. The generator reports type size in points, row count, repeated-copy count and actual body width.

4 · Export, then scan that actual output.

Selectable HTML preserves positioned visible letters. Letter RTF uses native text with exact line spacing. New words, URLs, fonts or sizes are untested outputs until scanned. Preserve the white margin and the named font.

Use the offline generator

What the tool guarantees

  • Whole source copies, in word order and original case; no partial final copy.
  • Exact payload retained or rejected; no shortened URL.
  • Visible selectable letters supply the QR ink. No hidden solid modules or image replacement.
  • Native measurements before layout, bounded word spacing and no automatic type shrinking.
  • Raw source, wrapped text, HTML, RTF and replayable recipe exports.

What still needs a real check

  • Whether a new text/payload pair scans on your target reader.
  • Receiving-app paste preserving font and line spacing.
  • Font installation and rendering on another operating system.
  • Physical printing, paper, lighting and repeat-attempt reliability.

Latin letters, precomposed accents, digits and punctuation are supported. Other scripts and combining marks are explicitly rejected. Arbitrary multilingual shaping is not implemented.

For documents, start with the saved Letter PDF or editable RTF. The RTF opened in TextEdit at the correct 9pt size and exact line spacing. Formatted HTML paste did not retain the same geometry. Word, Google Docs and other native receivers were not tested.

Passed: npm test, npm run build, npm run test:browser and npm run test:text-browser in a disposable copy. The maintained generator, interface, template, bundle-builder and final UI-check source pass their separate formatting check.

The final UI validation compares twelve saved exports exactly and tests the new full-text popup, raw CRLF source/payload import, source edits, MIME exports, stale-output disabling and five rejection paths.
